chunks: By my life, you continued drinking fresh milk every morning, And (continued) eating fine stoned dates with butter; We have given you the nobility which you did not possess before; And surrounded (protected) you with thoroughbred horses and tawnycoloured spears (strong spears).
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by 'you continued drinking fresh milk' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this verse from the Battle of the Camel, Imam Ali (AS) employs a rhetorical device of 'ungratefulness' to critique the Quraysh elite, contrasting their past comfort and his own prior lack of political dominance with his current burden of leadership. The mention of 'milk and dates' alludes to the material prosperity of the ruling class, while 'horses and spears' signifies the military apparatus now directed by Ali, underscoring the shift from passive nobility to active governance. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of Ali as the rightful successor who assumed the heavy responsibilities of the Caliphate despite the elite's prior complacency.
